notes: Strict, well-enforced 2016 NGO Act; English/French/Kinyarwanda; many expats operate through Rwandan partners rather than foreign registration. | Regulator is now Rwanda Governance Board (RGB), successor to MIDRRP; Law 01/2016 governs NGOs; official fee 300,000 RWF (~$24)

entity_types: ONG agréée
key_req: Prior approval from the Ministry of State for Humanitarian Affairs, local representative and local office; filings in French.
notes: Multiple foreign NGOs have been expelled; very high political risk; approvals are discretionary and often denied. | Governing law is Law 02/2017 on associations (plus 2017 ministerial ordinances); confirms very hard and politically risky

entity_types: NGO/CSO (local NGO or foreign NGO, NGO/CSO Act 2016)
key_req: Local NGOs need a Ugandan majority board; foreign NGOs register with Ministry of Internal Affairs with a resident legal representative and must route funds via Ugandan bank accounts.
notes: 2016 Act tightened foreign-funding rules; expats usually partner with a Ugandan-led CSO instead of foreign registration. | Confirm prior: NGO/CSO Act 2016, National NGO Bureau (ngobureau.go.ug), resident legal rep + local bank account requirements

entity_types: NGO (local/foreign, NGO Act as amended); trust
key_req: Two-thirds Tanzanian directors (2021 amendments); foreign-funded NGOs register with the NGO Commission; local office.
notes: 2021 amendments tightened foreign-funding thresholds and local-content rules; English/Swahili; NGO Commission is strict. | Core law is NGO Act (No. 22 of 2002, as amended); the 2021 tightening was a draft NGO Bill, not enacted law - earlier '2021 amendments' note overstated

entity_types: registered NGO (local organization or foreign organization, NGO Act 2003)
key_req: Foreign organizations need resident Kenyan directors, a KES 100,000 bank deposit and NGO Commission registration; local office.
notes: English-language, well-trodden expat route; many Australians register as foreign organizations; strong NGO infrastructure. | NGO Act 2003 was repealed - current framework is PBO Act, 2013 (Cap 134) under PBORA, not the NGO Commission/NGO Act route

entity_types: association déclarée; ONG agréée (2019 NGO law)
key_req: Foreign NGO approval from Ministry of Interior, local representative and local office; filings in French.
notes: Small islands, limited administrative capacity; political instability (2018 coup, 2024 elections); French required. | Main legal basis is Law 86-006/AF (1986) art. 9 plus Decree 20-101/PR of 31 July 2020 on NGO agrément; prior '2019 NGO law' reference is inaccurate

entity_types: association déclarée; ONG agréée
key_req: Foreign NGOs accredited via Ministry of Foreign Affairs with a local legal representative and local office; filings in French.
notes: No local-citizenship board rule; political instability since 2023; French-language process, local agent usable. | Confirm prior; core law is Law 96-030 (1996) + Decree 98-711; MFA accord de siege route confirmed by French diplomatic services page

entity_types: NGO (local/foreign, NGO Act 2005); trust
key_req: Local NGOs need a Zambian majority on the board; local office; English filings.
notes: Open, English, stable; expats commonly register local NGOs with Zambian directors; straightforward process. | Governing law is NGO Act No. 16 of 2009 (not 2005); Registrar sits in Ministry of Community Development and Social Services

entity_types: NGO (local/foreign, NGO Act 1997); trust
key_req: Local NGOs need a Malawian majority (two-thirds) board; local office; English filings.
notes: English-language, moderate bureaucracy; receiving foreign funds requires NGO registration. | Corrected: two-thirds Malawian board is not the rule - the Act requires >=2 Malawian-citizen directors/trustees; NGORA fee MK 35k + CONGOMA MK 55k; 2-8 weeks realistic

entity_types: ONG nacional / ONG estrangeira (2005 NGO law)
key_req: Foreign NGOs register with the Ministry of Foreign Affairs, with a Mozambican legal representative and local office; filings in Portuguese.
notes: Portuguese-language process; a hired local manager can serve as legal representative. | Confirm prior; core law is the NGO law (Lei 31/2002) with foreign-NGO regime via MFA; 2-6 months realistic; fee figure includes agent costs

entity_types: associação registada; ONG with local representative
key_req: Foreign NGO authorization from Ministry of Interior, local legal representative and local office; filings in Portuguese.
notes: Slow Portuguese-language bureaucracy; cautious approach needed for sensitive activities; few foreign charities register directly. | Confirm hard/3-12 months; note Lei do Estatuto das ONG (Law 2/26) now requires prior authorization for all NGOs; AOA 100k-500k = ~$100-500

entity_types: registered NGO (NGO Act); trust
key_req: Board of at least 3 members, local office and resident secretary; no citizenship restriction; English filings.
notes: Stable, English-language; straightforward but small-bureaucracy processing times. | Mostly confirm; common route is Societies Act (20+ members) or company limited by guarantee; resident director needed; P 500-1,500 = ~$25-75; 4-8 weeks

entity_types: non-profit society (Societies Act); public benefit trust (Deeds Registry)
key_req: No local-director requirement; local registered office/agent and English filings.
notes: English, registered agents widely available; a popular route for SADC-based charities; low regulatory burden. | Confirm prior; common route is Section 21 company via BIPA; local office + agent, no local director; NAD 300-1,000 = ~$20-70; 2-6 weeks | Verified: Documents must be notarized by a Namibian notary; non-resident directors allowed, a local agent can sign

entity_types: local/foreign NGO (NGO Act 2005); trust
key_req: Local NGOs need a two-thirds Zimbabwean board; foreign NGOs register with the Ministry of Local Government with a local representative; fees in USD.
notes: Political risk and restrictions on donor funding for certain activities; English language; many NGOs operate via local partnerships. | Corrected: governing law is the PVO Act [Ch 17:05], not an 'NGO Act 2005'; 2/3 Zimbabwean board for local PVO; US$100-500 and 1-4 months realistic

entity_types: non-profit society (Societies Act); NGO (foreign-fund registration)
key_req: Local office; registration with the Registrar of Societies plus NGO unit registration to receive foreign funds; English filings.
notes: Small, English-speaking; no local-director requirement; moderate small-country bureaucracy. | Corrected: NPOs currently registered under s17 Companies Act 8/2009, not a Societies Act; 2024 NPO Bill pending; SZL 500-2,000 = ~$25-90; 4-12 weeks

entity_types: non-profit society (Societies Act); trust
key_req: Local office; registration with the Ministry of Justice; English filings.
notes: Small, English-speaking; no local-director requirement; slow small-bureaucracy processing. | Confirm prior; routes: Societies Act, Companies Act 18/2011, Trusts Act; practitioners call registration easy; LSL 500-2,000 = ~$25-90

entity_types: non-profit company (NPC, Companies Act); trust (Trust Property Control Act); PBO (SARS)
key_req: No foreign restrictions; NCD online registration, local office/registered agent; English filings.
notes: Most open route in the region; NPO/NPC + trust + PBO gives donor tax-deductibility; strong expat charity infrastructure and English. | Confirm prior: CIPC NPC fee ZAR 125-175, no residency rule for directors but foreign directors use manual process; SA registered office required | Verified: Registration is voluntary and free; no residency requirement for founders; application filed at the nearest DSD office.

entity_types: Eingetragener Verein (e.V.), Gemeinnützige gGmbH, Private foundation (Stiftung, state law)
key_req: e.V. needs 7+ founding members, German registered office (Geschäftssitz in Germany), German-language articles; foreign founders/directors allowed without residency proof
notes: e.V. is the standard vehicle; charity status (gemeinnützig) confirmed later by Finanzamt; state register courts are slow; foundation endowments vary by state from ~EUR 10,000-25,000 | confirm prior; 7 members per section 56 BGB, no residency requirement, e.V. standard, charity status via Finanzamt | Verified: No residence requirement for board members; German seat needed; notarized application by the Vorstand.

entity_types: Eingetragener Verein (Verein), Private foundation (Stiftung, state-level law)
key_req: Verein needs 3+ founders, Austrian seat (local address), Austrian-language articles; no citizenship requirement for founders or board
notes: Verein is the practical vehicle; foundation laws are state-by-state (Landesrecht) with endowments from ~EUR 30,000-75,000; German required; charity tax recognition via Finanzamt | confirm prior; two-step process (errichtung then Genehmigung), 3 founders, no citizenship rule | Verified: No citizenship or residency requirement; district authority reviews within 4 weeks, extendable to 6

entity_types: Anstiftung (private foundation, 2013 law), Verein (association)
key_req: Foundation requires CHF 30,000 minimum endowment, seat in Liechtenstein, managing board seated locally (local officer/agent needed); German-language filings
notes: Small, stable, English-tolerant jurisdiction; local board presence makes it impractical without a local agent; no formal charity register; often paired with Swiss structures | confirm prior; CHF/EUR/USD 30,000 minimum endowment, founder may be any nationality, 0.1% annual charge (min CHF 1,000)

entity_types: Fondation (sovereign decree), Association (sovereign declaration)
key_req: Foundation requires EUR 50,000 minimum endowment and discretionary decree of the Prince on advice of the foundations commission; Monégasque registered office; French-language filings
notes: No formal charity category - establishment is discretionary sovereign approval; French required; popular with high-net-worth founders; no corporate income tax; in-person steps common | confirm; 1922 foundation law + 2008 association law (1355) apply; new patrimonial foundation route (FPI ~EUR 30k / FRUP ~EUR 100k) adds a streamlined option vs EUR 50k decree

entity_types: Fondazione (foundation), Associazione (association)
key_req: San Marino registered office; Italian-language filings; small opaque bureaucracy with in-person steps; endowment set by founding act for foundations
notes: Tiny jurisdiction with few foreign precedents and no English-language service; most foreigners use a neighbouring Italian (Emilia-Romagna) association instead; Italian required | confirm prior; note a dedicated private-foundation law is in legislative draft (2025), so foundations are still mainly set up ad hoc; associations already registrable with CGeG

entity_types: nezisková organizácia (nonprofit organization), verejne prospešná organizácia (VPO), nadácia (foundation)
key_req: Organization needs 2+ founders, local office and Slovak-language charter; foundation via notarized deed, endowment per charter; no citizenship requirement.
notes: VPO public-benefit status is a separate Ministry of Interior procedure; Slovak language barrier; paperwork moderate. | confirm prior; court registration fee ~150 EUR plus notary, so total ~200-600 EUR as noted

entity_types: udruženje građana (citizens' association), fundacija (foundation)
key_req: Association 3+ founders (foreigners allowed), local office, Montenegrin-language charter; no online registry, in-person/notarized steps.
notes: Slow bureaucracy, documents in Montenegrin, minimal English support; EU-candidate so framework is straightforward in principle. | Confirm association/foundation forms and 1-3 months; official gov.me page says registration is free, so prior 50-200 EUR is overestimated.

entity_types: udruženje (association), fundacija (foundation)
key_req: Association 3+ founders (foreigners allowed), local office, Macedonian-language charter; low fees.
notes: EU candidate, cheap and low-bureaucracy; language barrier for a resident-in-Australia founder means using a local agent/lawyer. | Confirm association/foundation and 1-2 months; state registration fee is nominal (~$0-50), prior 100-300 EUR overstates official cost.

entity_types: bashkimi (association), themelimin (foundation)
key_req: Association 3+ founders (foreigners allowed), local office, Albanian-language charter; new 2021 electronic register accepts applications by post/courier.
notes: 2021 NPO registration law modernized the register; English support limited; foreign-founded NGOs common, often with local partners. | Confirm association/foundation and 2021 electronic register; total all-in cost ~$300-550 incl. notary is consistent with prior.

entity_types: asociație (association), fundație (foundation)
key_req: Association 3+ founders (foreigners allowed), local office, Romanian-language charter (Russian widely used in practice); foundation 1 founder, endowment per charter.
notes: Cheap; EU candidate; political/economic volatility and weak enforcement; banking for foreign directors can be fiddly. | Confirm association/foundation and 2-6 weeks; no state registration fee (Lex Mundi guide), prior 100-300 EUR was notary/legal only.

entity_types: shtoprofitna asotsiia (public-benefit association), neprofitna pravno lice (nonprofit legal entity), fondatsiya (foundation)
key_req: Nonprofit legal entity (NPL) needs only 1 founder (foreigners allowed) + local office; association needs 5+ founders; Bulgarian-language documents.
notes: EU member; the 1-founder NPL form is the simplest for a lone foreign founder; good English support in Sofia; cheap to operate. | Confirm 1-founder NPL as simplest route; fees ~150-300 BGN plus notary; 30-day statutory limit as prior.

entity_types: syndesmos (association, general-benefit status), themelioma (foundation)
key_req: Association needs 5+ founders (foreigners allowed), Greek registered office, Greek-language charter filed with notary and court registry; foundation 1 founder, endowment per charter, notary deed.
notes: 2019 law modernized foundations, but process is paper/notary-heavy, Greek language required, no meaningful online registry; use a local lawyer. | Association min 7 founders (not 5); general-benefit status is a separate application after court registry filing. Confirm prior fees/timeline.

entity_types: Registered charity (Charity Commission for Ireland), company limited by guarantee (CRO), unincorporated charitable trust
cost_time: CRO company ~€100 + CCI registration free; ~4–8 weeks
key_req: Irish registered office and at least one EU-resident director/trustee; charities with income over €50k/yr must be registered with the Charity Commission for Ireland
notes: English-language, common-law system; no nationality requirement for trustees; most overseas founders set up a company limited by guarantee with a local registered-office agent, then register the charity | Confirm prior; regulator is the Charities Regulatory Authority (CRA), not the former 'Charity Commission for Ireland'.

entity_types: Nonprofit association (félag), foundation (stofnun), branch of foreign nonprofit (no formal 'charity' status)
key_req: Icelandic registered address and local contact; association needs ~5 members; foundation requires ~ISK 3m endowment and Icelandic management
notes: Documents in Icelandic; tax exemption (reykjafrjálsefni) must be applied for separately with the tax office; small bureaucracy but limited English support

entity_types: Unincorporated nonprofit association (ideell organisasjon), foundation (stiftelse), branch of foreign NGO
key_req: Norwegian address for the association (min. 3 adult members, no nationality rules); foundation needs ~NOK 1m capital and Norwegian-resident management
notes: Online via Altinn with English available; association is simple but requires a local contact; foundations have strict Norwegian-control rules | Prior cost corrected: initial association registration at Brønnøysund is free (not NOK 1,000-2,500).

entity_types: Nonprofit association (yhdistys), foundation (säätiö)
key_req: Finnish address; association needs min. 5 adult members; foundation needs €10k minimum capital, Finnish purpose, Finnish/Swedish-language operations and a Finnish-resident board
notes: Finnish-language requirement for documents and minutes; PRH bureaucracy is the main burden; foundations are hard for a foreign founder | confirm prior; PRH registration fee is about EUR 100.

entity_types: Nonprofit association (ideell förening), foundation (stiftelse)
key_req: Swedish registered seat (säte) and min. 3 members for the association, no residency requirement; foundation needs ~SEK 250k+ and a Swedish-resident board
notes: Straightforward online registration with Bolagsverket, English widely understood; a Swedish bank account for the entity typically requires a personal/D-number for the signatory

entity_types: Nonprofit association (forening), foundation (stiftelse), nonprofit company
key_req: Danish address, min. 2 members, registered in the CVR register; 2023 Foundation Act requires Danish-controlled foundations (Danish-resident board majority)
notes: Association name and documents must be in Danish; CVR registration itself is easy; Danish-controlled foundation rules make the foundation route hard for a foreigner

entity_types: Nonprofit organization (NVO, unified 2016-law form), foundation (dibinājums), religious organization
cost_time: State fee ~€30–100 plus notary costs; ~1–2 months
key_req: Latvian address, Latvian-language name/documents, and founding documents notarized by a Latvian notary before registration with the Enterprise Register
notes: The 2016 Nonprofit Organizations Law unified the forms; the notary step forces an in-person visit or a local representative, which is the main barrier for a foreign founder | NVO registers electronically via e-portals; no notary step needed. Real barriers: Latvian-resident board requirement plus local address and e-ID

entity_types: amuta (registered association), nonprofit corporation (amuta atzmit), public-benefit corporation (charitable amuta with DSD status)
key_req: 2-3 founders over 18 (Israeli citizenship NOT required), local Israeli registered agent/office, attorney-filed founding declaration and bylaws; English widely accepted

entity_types: association (jama'iyya) under Law 92/1996, private foundation (muassasa khassisa)
key_req: Foreigners CAN be founders and directors (no nationality rule) but need a local registered office, Arabic founding documents, and a local signatory; notification (declaration) regime, not pre-approval
notes: Legally one of the easiest for foreigners in the region, but heavy Arabic-only bureaucracy, bank-account opening friction, and macro instability (currency, banking) make practical setup harder; most internationals use a local registered partner or a foundation | Confirm prior: foreigners may found/direct, notification regime, 2-6 weeks; banking is the practical friction

entity_types: NGO/association (jam'iyya) under Law 12/2010, private foundation, branch of international NGO
key_req: Founding members must be Iraqi nationals or Iraq-resident; minimum 10 founders; local board, local address; Arabic filings; activity approvals from MoSAL
notes: Resident-expat route is the standard workaround (Iraqi-resident staff as founders); foreign funding rules restrict donor channels; English commonly understood in NGO sector but filings in Arabic; security considerations for in-person steps | Confirm prior: Law 12/2010 governs (new draft NGO law with 5 founders approved but 12/2010 still applied)

entity_types: association (NGO) under Law 19/2006, branch of international NGO
cost_time: A$200-500 fees, 4-8 weeks (gated by Bahraini board)
key_req: Founders must be Bahraini citizens (min. ~20) and board must be at least two-thirds Bahraini; local address; Arabic filings
notes: Bahrain is the most English-friendly and transparent NGO administration in the Gulf, but the nationality floor on founders/board keeps foreign formation out of reach; standard route is a partnership with an existing Bahraini NGO; government relations are comparatively accessible | Confirm prior: nationality floor (20 Bahraini founders, 2/3 board) keeps foreign formation out of reach; partnership route is standard.

entity_types: Registered association (Jamiyya, 2005 civil society law)
cost_time: ~US$100–300, 3–6 months, largely suspended due to conflict
key_req: Sudanese founders/chair, local office, Ministry of Culture & Information approval.
notes: 2023 civil war has paralysed registration bodies in most areas; acute security risk for foreign personnel; effectively unworkable right now. | Confirm prior: registration effectively suspended during conflict; Voluntary and Humanitarian Work Act is the restrictive governing law

entity_types: Registered association (Jam'iyya, Law 12/1989 as amended)
key_req: Libyan-national founders/chair, local office, ministry approval; registry split between rival governments in Tripoli and the east.
notes: Fragmented dual-government structure, militia influence, no workable foreign-formation path; foreign NGOs operate via UN/embassy channels only. | Confirm prior, with correction: current framework is NGO Law No. 19 of 2001 (and 2013 circulars), not Law 12/1989 as sole basis

entity_types: Declared association (Law 12-06/2012 on associations, amended 2020)
key_req: Local registered office, Arabic founding documents, declaration to the wilaya (provincial) authority; foreign founders heavily restricted.
notes: Strict regulation with security vetting for any foreign involvement; slow bureaucracy; Arabic required. | Confirm prior; Law 12-06 (2012) in force; 2025 replacement bill maintains prior authorisation and expands state control (not yet in force)

entity_types: Declared association (1959 law, amended 2011)
key_req: Registered office in Tunisia plus a local-resident representative (Tunisian, or foreigner resident in Tunisia); simple declaration to the prefecture.
notes: Most open civil-society law in the region; declaration-based, so registration is fast; post-2022 political centralisation adds compliance risk. | Confirm prior; governing text is Decree-Law 59-154 of 1959; only 2 founders needed; members 13+, must accept bylaws in writing

entity_types: Association (Law 1956 on association rights), nonprofit company (SPA)
key_req: Moroccan registered office, Arabic statutes, wilaya/provincial governor approval; foreign founders permitted.
notes: Governor discretion can delay approvals; most expats register via a local address agent; Arabic mandatory. | Confirm prior with correction: governing text is Dahir 1-58-376 of 1958 (not 'Law 1956'); foreign founders permitted; 1-3 months realistic

entity_types: Association (1965 Code of Associations)
key_req: Local registered office, meaningful local-national involvement, registration with the interior ministry; French/Arabic documents.

entity_types: None (no independent registry; Moroccan association law applies in Moroccan-administered areas)
key_req: Not available independently; the practical route is registering an association in Morocco.

entity_types: Ethiopian charitable organization (2021 NGO Proclamation), foreign NGO office via a local partner
key_req: Ethiopian-national founders for a domestic entity; a foreign founder must work through a partner organization or as a registered foreign NGO.

entity_types: None (no independent NGO law; state-controlled associations only)
key_req: No legal pathway for an independent foreign-founded charity.
notes: No legal space for independent civil society; all associations are state-controlled; high political risk. | Confirm prior: no legal pathway for an independent foreign-founded charity; state control confirmed by 2005 NGO Proclamation.

entity_types: Association (1971 law, as amended)
key_req: Local registered office, Djiboutian-national chair/meaningful involvement, interior-ministry registration; French/Arabic documents.
notes: Tight, security-driven regulation in a small country; English sometimes tolerated in practice; foreign aid actors mostly work through local partners. | Confirm prior: association law requires local involvement; cost ~$100-300 and 1-3 months plausible.

entity_types: Registered charitable organization/NGO (2013 federal NGO law)
key_req: Somali founders for a domestic entity; foreign NGOs register through embassy channel; local presence and security plan required.
notes: Severe insecurity and fragmented federal registries (Puntland, Somaliland, South West each have their own); foreign staff face high security risk. | Confirm prior: severe insecurity and fragmented registries; domestic charities need Somali founders; 3-6 months is optimistic, extend to 12.

entity_types: Registered association/NGO (2005 NGO law)
key_req: Local registered office and local partner involvement, registration with the interior/social-affairs ministry.
notes: De facto state without international recognition: banking, sanctions-compliance and repatriation risk; the civil-society registry is relatively functional and stable. | Confirm prior: 2010 NGO law (not 2005) governs; registry is relatively functional; cost 1-3 months plausible.

entity_types: Registered NGO (2009 NGO Act, amended 2018), domestic association
key_req: South Sudanese founders for a domestic entity; foreign NGOs register via embassy channel; local office required.
notes: Post-conflict, high security risk, weak institutions; most international actors work through established partners or missions. | Confirm prior, update: governing law is NGO Act 2016 (not 2009); 2023 amendment bill adds 80% local staff requirement; 6-12 months realistic.

entity_types: Non-profit organization (Non-Profit Organizations Act 2013), public-benefit foundation, non-profit limited company
key_req: Local registered office and licensed local agent; foreign directors permitted; registration with the Registrar of Companies.
notes: English-language, simple, offshore-friendly regime; popular with foreign founders; a Seychelles charity gains no local tax-exempt status without local operations. | Confirm prior: NPO Act 2013 for local NPOs; the practical foreign route is the Seychelles Foundation Act 2009 (SIBA, $200 gov fee); prior $1,500-3,000 is agent-inclusive. | Verified: No local presence required; foreign founder may be a councillor; FSA registration fee ~US$200 plus ~US$200 annual.

entity_types: Non-profit organization (NPO Act 2003), IFSA non-profit foundation, non-profit limited company
key_req: Mauritian registered office (local agent provides it); foreign founders/directors permitted; NPOs have a local-presence element.
notes: English-language with strong professional-services infrastructure; the IFSA foundation is the most foreigner-friendly route; popular expat-charity pathway. | Confirm prior: Foundations Act is 2012 (not 2014); NPO Act 2003 remains for local NPOs; $500-1,500 prior is agent-inclusive, gov fees are far lower.

entity_types: NGO registered under the NGO Act 1961, charitable trust, registered society
key_req: At least two-thirds of the NGO board must be Bangladeshi citizens (NGO Act 1961, s.3); local office and local officers required.
notes: Foreign founder cannot form an NGO without enough Bangladeshi citizens to fill 2/3 of the board. The 2016 NGO Ordinance restricts foreign-funded NGOs (derogatory-remarks clause) - ongoing political/legal risk for donor-funded charities. | confirm prior - NGO Act 1961 s.3 2/3 Bangladeshi-citizen board rule; 2016 Foreign Donations Act replaces 1978 Ordinance.

entity_types: Public charitable trust (registered with Registrar of Companies), society (Societies Ordinance), non-profit company
key_req: Trust deed with 2+ registered persons (3 recommended), local registered office; no citizenship requirement for trustees.
notes: Most expat-friendly in the region for a foreign founder; English is an official language. 12B tax-exempt status application to IRD follows trust registration. | confirm prior - trust route via Registrar-General (Trusts (Amend) Act 2018) confirmed; no citizenship requirement for trustees. | Verified: All international NGOs must register with the NGO Secretariat; MFA approval and a local address/agent required.

entity_types: Trust (Trust Act 2064), NGO (NGO Registration Act 2049, District Administration Office), registered society
key_req: NGO: board of 7 with at least 5 Nepali citizens, registration at the District Administration Office plus Social Welfare Council affiliation; Trust: 1+ settlor, foreign settlor permitted.

entity_types: NGO (NGO Act 2008 / NGO Trust Act 1997), trust
cost_time: Low fees, 2-8 weeks once a local sponsor is secured
key_req: Mandatory local Bhutanese sponsor/partner (FDI policy requires local partners; NGO registration requires a sponsoring agency).
notes: No direct foreign formation - a Bhutanese sponsor or partner organization is required. Small, tightly controlled NGO ecosystem; English used in official filings. | confirm prior - governing law is Civil Society Organizations Act 2007 (amended 2022), not 'NGO Act 2008'; no direct foreign formation.

entity_types: Public charitable trust (Public Trusts Act 1921, as amended, registered with MIRA), society, non-profit company
key_req: Trust registered with MIRA (Maldives Investment and Regulatory Authority) with 3+ trustees; practical requirement of resident local trustees and a Maldivian registered office.
notes: Most expats use the MIRA-registered public trust with local resident trustees and a local manager. English used in filings; annual returns and audited accounts required by MIRA. | confirm prior - public trust registered with Ministry of Justice; MIRA approval (MIRA 103) is for tax exemption, not registration.

entity_types: company limited by guarantee (CAC), trust (deed), NGO (NCMM-registered)
key_req: CAC registration of a company limited by guarantee with local resident directors/office, then registration with the NCMM (Nigerian Committee on Foreign Non-Governmental Organizations) and a Ministry of Interior Operational Readiness Certificate if receiving foreign funds
notes: Most structured path in West Africa but multi-layered; NCMM registration and ORC are the foreigner bottlenecks; English language; strong expat NGO sector in Lagos/Abuja

entity_types: company limited by guarantee, registered charity (Charities Commission, Act 1035 of 2020), trust
key_req: Charitable purpose with objects meeting the Charities Act test; Ghana Charities Commission registration; Ghana-located principal office (directors may be foreign)
notes: Most foreigner-friendly framework in the list: no local-national director requirement under the Companies Act 2019 (Act 992); Charities Commission registration has been operational since ~2021; English language

entity_types: association déclarée, fondation, organisation non gouvernementale (ONG)
key_req: Associations formed by declaration at the préfecture (Law n° 2022-443 of 15 Aug 2022 on OSCs) with local office; foreign-funded NGOs also need authorization from the Ministry of the Interior
notes: 2022 OSC law modernized the regime (declaration for associations, authorization for foreign-funded NGOs); French-only bureaucracy; Abidjan has active local law firms that handle expat NGO setups | OSC framework now Ordinance n° 2024-368 (12 June 2024) replacing Law 2022-443; eDA digital declaration portal live

entity_types: association déclarée, organisation non gouvernementale (ONG)
key_req: Declaration filed at the Direction de l'Administration Générale et des Cultes (Law n° 2015-04/PRB of 30 Jan 2016 on NGOs); local registered office; no local-national officer requirement
notes: One of the more open, stable regimes in francophone West Africa; French-only; Cotonou has NGOs/lawyers familiar with expat filings | New Decree 2025-636 (8 Oct 2025) regulates foreign NGO authorization and compliance declarations via CatIS portal

entity_types: association, organisation non gouvernementale (ONG)
key_req: Declaration/authorization of an association under Law n° 2000-17 of 11 Aug 2000 on NGOs; local registered office; French-language documents
notes: Administrative practice varies by préfecture; some steps in practice require in-person filing at the Mairie or prefecture in Lomé; French-only

entity_types: association (authorized), organisation non gouvernementale (ONG)
key_req: Prior government authorization under Law n° 014/1997-AN on associations; a 2018 constitutional amendment bars NGOs that receive foreign funding above a threshold from operating
notes: High political risk: 2018 constitutional ban on foreign-funded NGOs, 2022–2025 military rule, repeated suspensions of international NGOs (e.g. 2023–24 expulsions); effectively impractical for a foreign-funded charity | Association law replaced by Law n° 011-2025/ALT (17 July 2025, promulgated 23 July 2025); prior Law 014/1997 superseded

entity_types: association (loi 01-019 du 20 juin 2001), organisation non gouvernementale (ONG)
key_req: Association registration with the Direction de l'Administration Générale (Law n° 2001-019); local office; French-language filings; authorization regime for foreign-funded NGOs in practice
notes: Political instability (2020–2024 coups, ongoing conflict); security situation in many regions makes on-ground operations difficult; Bamako filings are French-only | Current association law is n° 04-038/ANRM (5 Aug 2004), which repealed Law 01-019 (2001) cited in prior context

entity_types: association (loi L/2010/004 du 3 janv 2010), organisation non gouvernementale (ONG)
key_req: Declaration of an association under Law L/2010/004; local registered office in Conakry; French-language documents
notes: 2010 association law uses a declaration regime (more open than the old authorization system); French-only; military rule since 2021 adds some political risk but NGO sector remains active | Association regime rests on loi 013/05 (2005) + L013 NGO text; prior 'loi L/2010/004 (2010)' not confirmed

entity_types: associação, organização não governamental (ONG)
key_req: Registration of an association under Lei n.º 5/VI/96 de 21 de Dezembro de 1996 (regime de registo); local office; Portuguese-language filings
notes: Repeated military coups (7 since independence), fragile state capacity, weak enforcement of registrations; Portuguese (not French) documents; practical operations very difficult | Prior cited Lei n. 5/VI/96 (1996) is superseded: Loi L/005/013/AN (2013) is the operative association law (repealed 1986 NGO decree)

entity_types: association déclarée (décret-loi de 1965, modèle 1901), organisation non gouvernementale (ONG)
key_req: Simple declaration of an association at the Direction de l'Action Sociale (1965 decree, French 1901 model); local registered office; French-language documents
notes: Stable, well-established association culture; declaration regime is the easiest in francophone West Africa; 2022/2023 framework on foreign-funded NGOs (OSC law) adds a reporting layer for foreign funders; French-only | Confirm prior: 1965 declaration regime (1901 model) stands; 2023 OSC framework confirmed as reporting layer, not a ban

entity_types: society (Societies Act, Cap 303), company limited by guarantee
key_req: Registration of a society with the Registrar of Societies under the Societies Act 1972 (or Companies Act 1964 for a CLG); local office; English-language filings
notes: English language, stable democracy; 2022 NGO Bill has been in draft years without enactment, so the old 1972 Societies Act still applies; Banjul filings manageable with a local agent | Confirm prior: Societies Act 1972 (Act No. 19 of 1972) still operative; NGO Bill still unenacted

entity_types: company limited by guarantee (Companies Act 2013), trust, charitable society
key_req: Registration of a non-profit company limited by guarantee with the Companies Registry; local registered office; English-language documents
notes: English language; 2022 NGO Bill pending, so existing NGO/charitable-society registration practices continue; Freetown has expat-friendly law firms; registry throughput is slower than Ghana | Confirm prior: Companies Act 2013 CLG route; NGO Bill 2022 still pending

entity_types: non-governmental organization (NGO Act 2015), limited liability company (non-profit), trust
key_req: NGO registration under the NGO Act of 2015 (Act No. 11 of 2015) with a local principal officer, local office, and a US$150 (local) fee; three-year permit renewal cycle
notes: English language; the 2015 Act is the operative law (it replaced the older NGO Bill regime); permits must be renewed every 3 years; local principal officer requirement is the main hurdle for a fully foreign board | Confirm prior: NGO Act 2015 operative, US$150 fee, 3-year renewal, local principal officer

entity_types: association (loi 93-010 du 28 avril 1993), organisation non gouvernementale (ONG)
